newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police to dig up grounds of "horror house".
newsitem.headline: Belgian police to dig up grounds of "horror house".

text.p: Police investigating a Belgian child sex ring said on Friday they would dig up the grounds of a "horror house" where two victims' bodies were found last September and which was burned down on Thursday night.

Work on excavating the site in Jumet, a suburb of Charleroi, would begin at first light on Saturday, police spokesman Guy Soumoy told a news conference held at a disused mine complex in the town which is also being searched.
The house was completely destroyed overnight in a blaze which fire services said was being treated as arson.
The house was last lived in by Frenchman Bernard Weinstein, an acquaintance of convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux who is chief suspect in Belgium's paedophile investigation.
The decomposed bodies of teenage friends An Marchal and Eefje Lambrecks, missing for a year, were found on September 4 last year under a shed in the grounds of the house.

Later that month more than 3,000 local people signed a petition clammering for the detatched property, which they dubbed the "House of Horror", to be razed to the ground and a memorial to the victims put in its place.
Meanwhile Soumoy said the mine complex search -- now in its 17th day -- would also continue until at least Monday night.
Police have gained access to ten underground mine galleries, of which three have so far been searched.

Soumoy said one of the galleries leads to a tunnel which was searched in October after Dutroux indicated victims may have been hidden there. The gallery appeared to connect with the tunnel beyond a wall of earth that led to the October search being abandoned.
Dutroux, who is in jail along with several alleged accomplices, has admitted abducting Marchal and Lambrecks as well as murdering Weinstein.
In August Dutroux led police to the bodies of two other girls -- Melissa Russo and Julie Lejeune -- buried alongside Weinstein in the garden of one of several houses Dutroux owned.
